title: Source Availability and Reproduction
paragraphs:
Appendix I
Source Availability and Reproduction
The available archive contains thesis sources, embedded chart coordinates,
and a demonstration-telemetry JSON summary. It does not include the platform
source tree, historical numerical engine, original R exports, respondent matrices,
transcripts, posterior draws, or trip statements mentioned in the inherited research
account.
No source inspection, native software test, respondent-level reanalysis,
or live platform experiment is certied by this version.
Earlier implementation
descriptions are historical reports requiring verication against a restored, versioned
archive.
I.1
What Can Be Reproduced Now
The supplied workow can compile the document, regenerate diagrams from shared
specications, inventory references and missing assets, hash available inputs, and
produce a reviewer package. These are document and arithmetic checks, not repli-
cations of the eld study. Generated synthetic xtures used to check software are
not participant records and never enter thesis results.

APPENDIX I. SOURCE AVAILABILITY AND REPRODUCTION
299
I.2
What Requires Additional Material
Field reproduction needs original questionnaire responses, the instrument and scor-
ing version, retained identiers, exclusion rationale, and analysis scripts. Qualitative
reproduction needs original records, their verbatim, translated, or reconstructed sta-
tus, the codebook, coding decisions, and consent-compatible access. Trip statements
document trips, not participant identity, informed consent, or attentive listening.
Historical simulation reproduction needs code, conguration, random-state deni-
tions, calibration particles, all run logs, and outputs; Bayesian reproduction also
needs priors, sampling settings, diagnostics, and posterior draws.
I.3
Implementation and Measurement Boundaries
A route name, test function, screenshot, or container specication does not estab-
lish successful treatment delivery. Before the prospective experiment, verify each
active feature against its versioned implementation and reconcile acknowledged ac-
tions with archived events and committed state. Isolate condition-specic accounts,
databases, media state, and message streams. Keep eld responses, synthetic ac-
counts, and demonstration telemetry separate.
Theoretical BRS components, a platform feedback posterior, and the 11-item
questionnaire are dierent objects. Agreement among their names cannot establish
equivalent scoring or validated uncertainty.
The historical replication-percentile
intervals and equal-tailed Bayesian intervals likewise retain distinct interpretations
(Section 5.17).
